brief: Aggressive. The identity is a wolf's claw raking across a heavy black wordmark in hot crimson — the site should feel like that, not like the navy agency template currently in front of it. Two things carry the whole design: the four-streak claw as a structural motif, and personalization (named, photographed humans instead of an anonymous call centre).

sources.used_for: accent colour sampled from the claw itself (#EA0A2A, 1369 opaque pixels), wordmark black, claw geometry
font families (Montserrat display / Source Sans Pro body), 0px radius convention
sources.anti_pattern_lock: no layout, section rhythm, component styling, or screenshot was taken from this source

sources.used_for: owl section order and component inventory

contrast_audit.note: All measured with the owl README method. AA text threshold 4.5:1.
contrast_audit.why_three_accents: The claw crimson is the textbook case the owl tokens.css comment describes: #EA0A2A clears AA as a button fill under white text (4.59) but is only 4.59 as text on white and would be unreadable inside the black bands. #C4001B is the text-on-light variant, #FF5A6E the text-on-black variant. The fill colour never changes, so the red the eye reads as 'the Wolfpack red' is identical site-wide.

typography.rationale: Both are the client's own brand fonts. Montserrat at 800/900, uppercase, with tight negative tracking approximates the heavy condensed wordmark in the logo and carries the aggression without importing a novelty face.
typography.treatment: Headings uppercase, weight 800-900, letter-spacing -0.02em. Eyebrows uppercase, weight 700, letter-spacing 0.14em, in accent_ink on light and accent_on_dark on black.

radius.rationale: The client's existing buttons are square (0px). Sharp corners read as aggressive; rounding would soften exactly the wrong thing.

motion.allowed: Short, decisive transitions (120-180ms, ease-out). Claw streaks may sweep in on scroll where the CSS is cheap.
motion.banned: Parallax, autoplaying carousels, anything longer than 300ms, bounce easing.

signature_motif.name: The Claw
signature_motif.spec: Four parallel bars, raked 20deg from vertical, tapered at both ends, in #EA0A2A. Widths run 6px / 10px / 10px / 6px so the outer two read as the thinner outside claws, matching the logo.
placements: Section divider between every major band — a full-bleed rake of four streaks on the seam.
Hero: an oversized, low-opacity claw raked across the right side of the dark hero, behind the headline.
Numbered process steps: the step number sits inside a claw slash instead of a circle.
Card hover: the four streaks sweep across the top edge of a service card.
Section eyebrows: a miniature four-streak glyph replaces the usual bullet or rule.
signature_motif.restraint: It is a rake, not wallpaper. Never more than one large claw per viewport, and never behind body copy at an opacity that costs contrast.

personalization_direction.why: Ghosting and rotating anonymous crews are the #1 and #5 documented complaints in the local research. Wolfpack has seven named, photographed staff and a family-owned story — the strongest available counter.
how: A named-team band ('Meet The Pack') on the home page, not buried three levels into the nav.
Hero quote card attributed to a real reviewer with the 4.9 / 63 rating attached.
Process copy written in first person plural with a named point of contact promise.
The CGC licence number printed in plain sight rather than implied.

anti_patterns: No gradient hero backgrounds — flat black with a photo scrim only.
No glass morphism or backdrop-blur panels.
No purple/indigo/violet anywhere — the palette is black, white, and one crimson.
No rows of outline icons; at most one icon per section and only where it carries meaning.
No stock handshake / hardhat-closeup / team-pointing-at-laptop photography — the client's own project and staff photos only.
No invented review counts, prices, or project totals.
No navy. The old site's slate-blue chrome is the specific thing being replaced.
No rounded pill buttons — square edges only.
No randomized section order; owl's fixed order is authoritative.
